summary:
Split the path on `/` and process the parts with a stack of folder names: empty parts and `.` change nothing,
`..` pops (if anything is there), and every other name is pushed. Join the stack with `/` behind a leading `/`.
O(n).

question.md:
Rewrite an absolute path into its tidy form: single slashes, no `.` or `..`, no trailing slash (except the root
itself).

- **`..` at the root stays at the root:** `/../a` → `/a`.
- **`...` is just a folder name**, as is anything that isn't exactly `.` or `..`.
- **Repeated slashes collapse:** `/a//b` → `/a/b`.

think.md:
Take `/usr//local/./bin/../lib/.../`. Reading folder by folder: `usr`, `local`, `.` (stay), `bin`, `..` (back out of bin), `lib`,
`...` (a normal name). Result: `/usr/local/lib/...`.

think.caption: Empty parts come from repeated or trailing slashes.

think.md: `..` undoes the most recently entered folder: last in, first out. That's a stack of folder names.

approaches.title: Rewrite the text until it stops changing

idea.md: Apply local rewrite rules repeatedly: collapse `//`, delete `/./`, cancel `/name/../`, and turn a leading `/../` into `/`. When nothing applies, trim the trailing slash.

build: Append `/` so every part is surrounded by slashes.
Loop over the rules until a full round changes nothing.
Remove the trailing `/` (keep `/` for the root).

lines.text: A trailing `/` makes every part, including the last, look like `/part/`.
Local simplifications: empty part (`//`), `.` part, `name/..` pair, and `..` right at the root.

notes.cpp: One scan finds the first part that is empty, `.` or `..`, and removes it (for `..`, together with the folder before it, unless it's at the root).

complexity.md: **Time O(n²):** each rewrite rescans and shifts the string. **Space O(n).**

steps.text: Add a trailing '/' so every part is wrapped in slashes: /usr//local/./bin/../lib/...//

walk.title: Repeatedly apply text rewrites: '//' → '/', '/./' → '/', '/name/../' → '/', until nothing changes.

limits.md: Each fix rescans from the start. The structure is just "enter folder / leave folder", which a stack processes in one pass.

approaches.title: Split, then a stack of folders

idea.md: Split on `/`. For each part: empty or `.` → nothing; `..` → pop if non-empty; else push. Answer: `/` + parts joined by `/`.

build: Process parts with the stack rules.

lines.text: Folder names currently entered, deepest last.

notes.c: The stack stores where each kept name starts in the input and how long it is; no copying until the end.

lines.text: Pieces between slashes; repeated or trailing slashes produce empty pieces.

notes.cpp: `getline` with `'/'` as the delimiter yields each piece.
notes.c: Skip slashes, then take the run of non-slash characters as the next piece.

lines.text: `..` leaves the current folder; at the root there's nothing to leave.
Anything else that isn't empty or `.` is a folder to enter (including `...`).
Rebuild with single slashes; an empty stack is the root `/`.

complexity.md: **Time O(n).** **Space O(n)** for the parts and the result.

takeaways.md:
- Path normalisation = **stack of components**: push names, pop on `..`, ignore `.` and empty parts.
- Split first; work with tokens rather than characters.
